item.title: Issue #3038 created
item.description:
Align record-declaration constraints with the definition of err:XPST0003

The specification of err:XPST0003 says:

err:XPST0003

It is a static error if an expression is not a valid instance of the grammar defined in A.1 EBNF.

But recent changes to record declarations call for issuing err:XPST0003 in cases conforming to the grammar:

  • for labeled records with constructor functions (§5.20.2):

    The names of the fields must be simple NCNames in no namespace; the names must not be written as string literals [err:XPST0003]. Note: This is described here as a semantic constraint, but an implementation might choose to impose it at the level of the grammar.

  • for fields declared as %static (recordTypeDecl-137): 
    <test-case name="recordTypeDecl-137" covers-40="PR2979">
   <description>Static field must have an initial value</description>
   <created by="Michael Kay" on="2026-10-29"/>
   <test><![CDATA[
      declare record local:rectangle(x, y, %static area);
      local:rectangle(4, 5) =?> area()
   ]]></test>
   <result>
      <error code="XPST0003"/>
   </result>
</test-case>

The grammar fragment that covers both cases is this:

ExtendedFieldDeclaration ::= "%static"? FieldDeclaration (":=" ExprSingle)?
FieldDeclaration         ::= FieldName ("as" SequenceType)?
FieldName                ::= NCName | StringLiteral

It currently unconditionally allows both StringLiteral as FieldName, and uninitialized static fields.

To keep the record declaration rules aligned with the definition of err:XPST0003, my proposal is:

  • to define a dedicated static error code for the case where a record declaration that generates a constructor function contains a field name written as a string literal. The accompanying note should be removed or revised accordingly.
  • to make the initializing expression mandatory for %static fields in the grammar: 
    ExtendedFieldDeclaration ::= FieldDeclaration (":=" ExprSingle)?
                           | "%static" FieldDeclaration ":=" ExprSingle
    This preserves optional initialization for non-static fields and makes a missing initializer on a static field a grammar violation.
